cards.explanation: The answer is silence for about half an hour. "When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour." The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven goes quiet. I'd have checked whether my ears were still working.

The answer is the prayers of all the saints. The angel is given much incense to offer, "…along with the prayers of all the saints, on the golden altar before the throne." Those prayers aren't tucked in a corner. They're right there with the incense at the altar before the throne. I think that's worth a slow, happy nod.

The answer is False. The text says the smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of the saints, “…rose up before God from the hand of the angel.” Nothing fades on the way. The prayers go up from the angel's hand and arrive before God.

The answer is that he hurls it to the earth. The angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and “…hurled it to the earth…” That's not a gentle toss. It lands with thunder, lightning and an earthquake, and the text says all of that in one breath.

The answer is True, and the text packs it in. When the censer is hurled to the earth, there are "…peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake." That's sound, light and shaking in one list. I'd have grabbed the counter.

The answer is hail and fire mixed with blood. When the first angel sounded his trumpet, "…hail and fire mixed with blood were hurled down upon the earth." Hail and fire don't usually travel together, and the text adds blood on top. It's a heavy picture, and the text doesn't soften it.

The word is burned. The text says, "A third of the earth was burned up, along with a third of the trees and all the green grass." That's what happens when the first angel sounds his trumpet, and hail and fire mixed with blood are hurled down upon the earth. I've burned a batch or two myself, but never a third of the earth.

The answer is True. Look at the wording: a third of the earth and a third of the trees, then "…all the green grass." Most of the list says a third, but the grass says all. Good thing to notice, friends.

The answer is that a third of the ships are destroyed. The text says "…a third of the ships were destroyed." It comes right after a third of the sea turns to blood and a third of the living creatures in the sea die. So the ships on that sea are struck too, friends, and the text says it plainly.

The answer is False. With the second trumpet, the text says "…a third of the living creatures in the sea died…" So the claim that every one survives doesn't match what the text says. It's a heavy line, and I won't pretend it isn't.

The answer is False. The text says a third of the waters turned bitter, and "…many people died from the bitter waters." So the claim that no one is harmed doesn't match the verse. It's a hard line, and I think it deserves a quiet moment.

The answer is that a third of day and night go dark. "A third of the stars were darkened, a third of the day was without light, and a third of the night as well." That's what happens when the fourth angel sounds his trumpet and a third of the sun and moon and stars are struck. So a third of the day goes without light, and a third of the night does too. That's a whole lot of dark to land on one clock.

The answer is the trumpets of the last three angels. The eagle cries, "Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the trumpet blasts about to be sounded by the remaining three angels!" Four trumpets have sounded and three are left. That's the warning.
